source.title: InverseScope: Scalable Activation Inversion for Interpreting Large Language Models
source.authors: Yi-Fan Luo; Zhen-Nan Zhou; Bin Dong

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses assumptions behind sparse dictionary methods and reports results about LLM activation geometry, but it does not test feature superposition, capacity-driven polysemanticity, SAE features, or feature dimensionality as described by the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The sentence-analogy and refusal-ablation findings concern activation geometry, but do not measure whether sparse features overlap, how features compete for capacity, or whether model features are one-dimensional. Retrieval-efficiency and scaling results evaluate InverseScope, not the claim. The refusal-direction result is a study result, not a cited result; the prior claim that refusal is mediated by one direction is cited background.
record.test_reason: The paper introduces an activation-inversion method (InverseScope) and only discusses sparse dictionary learning's assumptions as motivation. Its case studies (sentence-level analogy, refusal-direction ablation) concern activation geometry in Qwen3 models. They do not measure feature overlap, capacity competition, polysemantic neurons, SAE feature recovery, or feature dimensionality. The remaining results (retrieval efficiency, scaling) evaluate the method itself. No version of the claim is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that InverseScope is an assumption-light inversion method that scales to 14B models and recovers sentence-level linear analogies. They also conclude it makes the effect of refusal-direction ablation legible in natural language. They draw no conclusion about superposition.
record.recipe_differences: InverseScope is a conditional activation-inversion method using control layers to sample inputs near target activations; it does not reproduce the Toy Models of Superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that retrieval quality varies with the InverseScope backbone size; target-model size has approximately flat validation loss across the tested models. These are method-performance findings, not tests of the claim.

fits_no_version.finding: For woman − man + king at the last token, layer 16 of Qwen3-4B, 'The queen stood alone upon the shore.' was the nearest generated sentence (L2 0.1117).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LLM sentence activations preserve linear analogy structure.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating the refusal direction shifted the inverted neighborhood from fraudulent-letter requests to benign letter requests. This is a single example.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The refusal direction also carries a semantic signal of harmful intent.

record.peer_reviewed: Mechanistic Interpretability Workshop at the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, 2026 (as stated in the paper); the supplied metadata lists arXiv.org.
record.problems: The paper says its interpretability utility is limited to case studies and that it lacks a quantitative method for using inverse-based methods in interpretability studies. No uncertainty estimates are stated for the reported results.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the claim versions. Retrieval-efficiency comparisons and scaling-loss results were not included because they evaluate InverseScope rather than feature superposition or the other listed claim versions.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, sparsity sweep, or feature geometry measured.
All: no measure of feature importance or capacity allocation.
All: polysemantic neurons are not examined.
All: no neuron-level spread or SAE recovery measured. Sparsity is only questioned in the introduction.
All: SAE features are not trained or evaluated.
All: Engels et al. is only cited. No test of multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: Both rows are correctly linked to 'none'. Row r2's subject is listed as Qwen3-4B; the main text specifies Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 as the default target. Both results are single case studies with no uncertainty reported.

versions.untested_parts: Whether sparse features outnumber dimensions, overlap as nearly orthogonal directions, or exhibit sparsity-dependent transitions and regular geometry.
Whether feature importance and limited capacity cause dedicated dimensions for some features and sharing for others.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise for reasons other than capacity pressure, or whether polysemanticity evidences superposition.
Whether LLM features spread across neurons or sparse features can be recovered with a dictionary or SAE.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, canonical units of model representations.
Whether superposed features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.

rows.subject: Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507
rows.operation_detail: Tested sentence-level vector analogy by conditioning on z(woman) − z(man) + z(king) and ranking generated sentences by L2 distance.

conditions.value: The {woman/man/king/queen} stood alone upon the shore.

rows.measure: Rank and L2 distance of generated prompts from the target activation.
rows.value: “The queen stood alone upon the shore.” ranked first, with L2 distance 0.1117.
rows.note: The paper says this confirms sentence-level linear analogy structure; this does not test feature superposition or feature dimensionality.

rows.subject: Qwen3-4B
rows.operation_detail: Ablated the refusal direction from the layer-16 residual-stream activation using orthogonal projection, then inverted the original and ablated activations.

conditions.value: one harmful instruction; exact instruction not stated
original activation z versus refusal-direction-ablated activation z̃

rows.measure: Semantic content of nearest-neighbor input prompts in the activation neighborhood.
rows.baseline: Neighborhood of z was dominated by fraudulent and deceptive letter requests.
rows.value: Neighborhood of z̃ shifted entirely to benign letter-writing requests.
rows.note: The authors interpret the shift as indicating that the direction carries a semantic signal of harmful intent. This is not a test of superposition or the dimensionality of features.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
